question: Should OpenClaw make operator-selected core readiness criteria and plugin-registered readiness observations a supported core and plugin-SDK contract, or keep readiness limited to the existing Gateway lifecycle checks?
rationale: This is a broad new configuration and plugin API surface rather than a narrow repair, and neither a mechanical patch nor tests can determine the long-term supported contract and upgrade posture.

options.title: Sponsor the readiness contract
options.body: Accept the operator-selected readiness and plugin-provider model, land the foundation first, then require this follow-on to rebase and prove the final integrated behavior.

options.title: Narrow to Gateway-owned checks
options.body: Keep readiness as an internal Gateway lifecycle feature and remove the new plugin SDK registration and broad owner-criteria surface.

options.title: Pause pending RFC decision
options.body: Leave the stack unmerged until the linked RFC and foundation proposal receive explicit project direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the readiness contract
recommendation.body: Accept the operator-selected readiness and plugin-provider model, land the foundation first, then require this follow-on to rebase and prove the final integrated behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked foundation and follow-on stack and can clarify the proposed contract; final acceptance remains a project-owner decision.
